subject: SCCs + UK IDTA: onboarding playbook and subprocessors
messages:
From: Tanya Singh <tanya.singh@paylance.co.uk>
To: evelyn_hart <evelyn.hart@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Rory Blake <rory.blake@paylance.co.uk>, LegalOps <legalops@paylance.co.uk>
Date: Wed, 10 Jun 2026 13:05:00 +0100
Subject: Redwood SCCs/UK IDTA questions for onboarding

Hi Evelyn,

Thanks for the demo yesterday — our procurement and legal teams are starting the vendor onboarding. Two quick items we need from Redwood before we proceed:

1) A current list of subprocessors and whether any of them are outside the UK/EU (we need location details and whether they process identifiable logs).
2) Your position on the EU SCCs + the UK IDTA / UK Addendum. Will Redwood sign the UK IDTA addendum or do you expect counterparties to rely on SCCs alone?
3) If Redwood requires a TIA/DTIA for any downstream analytics vendors, can you flag that now?

Can you send the documents and an outline of the next steps (who needs to sign, typical timelines)? We ideally want this wrapped up for the PO by end of month.

Best,
Tanya
Tanya Singh
Head of Legal Ops — PayLance Ltd.
attachments: none

From: evelyn_hart <evelyn.hart@redwoodinference.com>
To: Tanya Singh <tanya.singh@paylance.co.uk>
Cc: Rory Blake <rory.blake@paylance.co.uk>, karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>, neha_kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>, aditya_rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 10 Jun 2026 14:22:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Redwood SCCs/UK IDTA questions for onboarding

Hi Tanya — great to hear from you and thanks for the clear list.

High level: Redwood is prepared to execute the EU Standard Contractual Clauses (SCCs) and we offer a UK IDTA addendum for UK-hosted customers where required. I'm looping in our Legal team (Karthik and Neha) to confirm specifics and to attach the current docs.

Next steps from our side:
- I'll send the SCCs + current subprocessors inventory (CSV) and a draft UK IDTA addendum for your review (please see attachments once legal confirms).
- Karthik can confirm whether any subprocessors will require TIAs/DTIAs (e.g., analytics vendors that receive pseudonymized logs).
- If PayLance prefers DocuSign, we can prepare the signing packet. Typical timeline: 3–7 business days after redlines are agreed for legal, faster if no redlines.

Could you confirm the procurement contact and whether PayLance is requesting UK-only data residency or just the contractual UK safeguards? That will affect whether we bundle the IDTA or leave it optional.

I'll come back with the attachments shortly.

Thanks,
Evelyn Hart
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference, Inc.
attachments: SCCs pending, subprocessors pending

From: karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: Tanya Singh <tanya.singh@paylance.co.uk>, evelyn_hart <evelyn.hart@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: neha_kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>, aditya_rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 11 Jun 2026 09:10:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Redwood SCCs/UK IDTA questions for onboarding

Tanya / team — thanks for escalating. Quick legal summary and attachments attached.

- EU SCCs: Redwood executes the EU Standard Contractual Clauses. Please note the SCCs we use are the current 2021 wording; we've included the signed template (Redwood_SCCs_2026.pdf).

- UK IDTA: We offer a UK IDTA addendum (attached as UK_IDTA_Addendum_draft.docx). For UK data subjects, we can append the UK addendum and execute it alongside the DPA. The addendum covers the same core commitments as SCCs but is packaged for UK contracting teams.

- Subprocessors: Our up-to-date inventory is subprocessors_inventory_2026.csv. Highlights: CloudStor Analytics (US), ObjectVault Storage (US, EU replicas), EU-Monitoring (EU). The inventory indicates whether a subprocessor receives logs or pseudonymized identifiers.

- TIAs / DTIAs: We do not proactively execute standalone TIAs for every downstream vendor. We will flag TIAs where a subprocessor (e.g., CloudStor Analytics) receives persistent, identifiable logs that could constitute onward transfer risk. For PayLance's use case, based on the data elements discussed in the demo, CloudStor Analytics would receive pseudonymized telemetry only — we flag it as a candidate for a limited TIA scope (pseudonymized analytics).

Operational notes:
- Notification window for subprocessor additions: 30 days (business practice; contractual notice is 30 days unless an exception for emergency security updates).
- Data residency options: Redwood can be configured to prefer EU-only replicas for model inputs/outputs if PayLance requires. That is a product-level configuration and not a contractual restriction (we would encode the preference in the DPA/IDTA).

Please review the attachments and send any redlines. If PayLance prefers, we can produce a DocuSign packet next week.

Regards,
Karthik Iyer
Head of Legal — Redwood Inference
attachments: Redwood_SCCs_2026.pdf; UK_IDTA_Addendum_draft.docx; subprocessors_inventory_2026.csv

From: Rory Blake <rory.blake@paylance.co.uk>
To: karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>, evelyn_hart <evelyn.hart@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Tanya Singh <tanya.singh@paylance.co.uk>, LegalOps <legalops@paylance.co.uk>
Date: Fri, 12 Jun 2026 08:03:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Redwood SCCs/UK IDTA questions for onboarding

Hi Karthik — thanks for the rapid response and the documents. A few clarifying questions from our side after reviewing the inventory:

1) CloudStor Analytics: you flag it as US-based and receiving pseudonymized telemetry. Can you confirm whether any identifiers are reversible (i.e., can CloudStor correlate telemetry with internal PayLance PII)? If reversible, we'll need a TIA.

2) DocuSign method: PayLance legal prefers DocuSign for signature. Can you confirm Redwood will prepare the signing packet and send to legalops@paylance.co.uk?

3) Emergency subprocessor exceptions: you mentioned a 30-day notice window — can you confirm the contract clause also covers emergency security patches where notification might be post-facto? PayLance's security team requires explicit language around that.

If those answers are positive we can proceed to PO and target an implementation window late June.

Thanks,
Rory
Head of Procurement — PayLance Ltd.

From: evelyn_hart <evelyn.hart@redwoodinference.com>
To: Rory Blake <rory.blake@paylance.co.uk>, Tanya Singh <tanya.singh@paylance.co.uk>
Cc: karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>, neha_kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>, aditya_rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 12 Jun 2026 09:15:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Redwood SCCs/UK IDTA questions for onboarding

Rory / Tanya — quick answers and actions from our side: 

- CloudStor Analytics: Karthik confirms pseudonymized telemetry only; no reversible identifiers are sent by default. We'll include a specific TIA clause scoped to "pseudonymized analytics telemetry" in the DPA addendum to be explicit.

- DocuSign: yes — we'll produce a DocuSign packet. Expected recipients: legalops@paylance.co.uk + primary PO contact. I'll prepare the envelope and share the link (we'll use the linked signing URL in related_links).

- Emergency exceptions: contract will include the standard emergency subprocessor clause: Redwood may engage a subprocessor for emergency security or stability reasons with post-notification and a remedial risk assessment; we will not use emergency exceptions to change the overall transfer basis. Karthik / Neha to add the exact clause text in the final DPA.

Action items:
1) Karthik / Neha: insert TIA-scoped language and emergency clause into UK_IDTA_Addendum_draft.docx and return to Evelyn by EOD Mon.
2) Evelyn: prepare DocuSign envelope and share link to legalops@paylance.co.uk once doc is final.
3) PayLance: confirm PO contact for signature and billing.

I'll follow up next week with the DocuSign link. Thanks all.

Best,
Evelyn
attachments: none
